title: He heard about Jesus…
paragraphs: …and still wondered if He was real.

The man who baptized Christ…
the man who saw heaven open…
the man who declared, “Behold, the Lamb of God”…
now whispers from a prison cell:
“Are You the one… or should we look for another?”
Because this is where it gets uncomfortable—
Sometimes the strongest believers don’t lose faith in public…
Because your obedience didn’t produce the outcome you expected.
and now you’re the one suffering for it.
you started asking a dangerous question:
“Jesus… are You really who I thought You were?”
We don’t talk about this part of faith.
What about the delay that doesn’t make sense?
John wasn’t in prison because he sinned.
He was in prison because he obeyed.
Sometimes your suffering is not a sign of disobedience…
But here’s where shame creeps in.
“If I’m doubting… maybe I’m not really saved.”
Because this will break every lie shame ever told you.
📖 “Are You the one who is to come, or shall we look for another?” — Matthew 11:3
Doesn’t say, “After all you’ve seen, you dare question Me?”
📖 “Go and tell John what you hear and see: the blind receive their sight and the lame walk, lepers are cleansed and the deaf hear, and the dead are raised up…” — Matthew 11:4–5
Some scholars interpret this moment not as unbelief—but as a crisis of expectation.
John knew the Messiah would come in power.
“Why doesn’t it look like what I expected?”
And that’s where many of us live.
Because He didn’t heal the way we wanted.
Didn’t move according to our timeline.
But here is the Gospel turn.
Jesus did not come first to fix your circumstances.
He came to save your soul.
John was looking for a political deliverer.
But Jesus came first as a sin-bearer.
Because your greatest prison is not external.
And no amount of answered prayers can fix that.
Only the blood of Jesus can.
This is the truth we avoid:
And Jesus didn’t come to make your life comfortable.
He came to make you new.
📖 “Blessed is the one who is not offended by me.” — Matthew 11:6
Because many don’t walk away from Jesus because He is false…
but because He is not what they wanted.
Your desire for a God who serves you…
instead of a God you surrender to.
He does not push away the one who comes honestly.
And here’s the part that will wreck you.
Jesus turns to the crowd and says:
📖 “Among those born of women there has arisen no one greater than John the Baptist.” — Matthew 11:11
did not erase a lifetime of faithfulness.
Let that heal something in you.
Your struggle doesn’t cancel your calling.
Your doubt does not delete your devotion.
Where He would not question the Father—
The ones we never talk about.
who repents and believes in Him…
would not stay in their prison.

your doubt,
your disappointment,
your unmet expectations—
And trust Him not because life makes sense…
but because the cross proves He is faithful.
Are you offended by the way God is working in your life?
Or are you willing to trust Him—even when it hurts?
Will you walk away because He didn’t meet your expectations…
or will you surrender because He exceeded your need?
